newsitem.title: USA: Denmark offers to host debt Trust Fund meeting.
newsitem.headline: Denmark offers to host debt Trust Fund meeting.

text.p: The Nordic countries welcome the initiative to reduce the debt burden of the poorest countries and would be willing to contribute to the initiative through the proposed Trust Fund, Denmark's Developmental Aid Minister Poul Nielson said.

In a speech prepared for delivery to the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, Nielsen issued an invitation on behalf of the Danish government for an inaugural meeting of the Trust Fund to be held in Copenhagen.
"The early convening of a founding meeting will demonstrate a firm political determination to carry forward the initiative," Nielson, speaking on behalf of the Nordic countries, said.
The proposed Trust Fund is intended to be made up of money from the World Bank's profits and also funds from outside contributors. It will be used to help debt-laden nations.
"There is willingness among the Nordic countries to contribute to the Initiative through the proposed Trust Fund, and we expect others to contribute their share," Nielson said.

The Nordic countries said the debt initiative agreed in Washington should now be implemented as a matter of urgency. The modalities for burden sharing between bilateral and multilateral creditors should now be quickly resolved.

It welcomed the decision by the Paris Club to forgive up to 80 percent of poor country's debt on a case-by-case basis, but added the decision was "not as bold as we had hoped for." The Paris Club nations had originally been called on to forgive up to 90 percent of outstanding debt in special cases.
